- [statement] The authors report that secondary and exploratory clinical outcomes showed improvement or stability, including improvement in the MDS-UPDRS Part III OFF scores by an average of 23 points in the high-dose cohort, in this open-label early-phase trial. ## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] In the Movement Disorders systematic review of neuroimaging-based AI studies, the authors report that the majority of studies aimed to distinguish PD patients from healthy controls (54%) or atypical parkinsonian syndromes (25%), whereas prognostic or interventional studies were sparse. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11657025/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] Reviews report inconsistent validation practice in PD machine learning: in one sample of 113 studies only 65.5% (74/113) used a holdout test set to avoid potentially inflated accuracies and 38.9% (44/113) did not report on how or if models were tuned, and a review of machine learning within PPMI finds significant variability in the types of data, models, and validation procedures used across studies. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11112052/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9968811/
- [statement] Neuroimaging-focused reviews flag quality and translation concerns: the Movement Disorders review reports that only 20% of evaluated studies passed all five MQC and calls the number of studies failing to pass the MQC alarming, a brain-imaging machine learning review states that several issues must be addressed before these solutions can be safely integrated into clinical practice, and a deep learning review identifies a lack of data availability and interpretability of models. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11657025/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10394631/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37200116/
- [statement] External validation is uncommon in the reviewed literature: the neuroimaging review reports that very few studies employed external test sets (8%), where accuracy was significantly lower, and the later biomarker review reports that only 20 (7.6%) of the studies met its external-validation definition and that in ten within-study comparisons external performance fell in eight. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11657025/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13702696/
- [statement] Deep learning is not uniformly superior: a review of deep learning in PD reports state-of-the-art performance in many PD-related tasks by outperforming conventional machine learning approaches, while a gait meta-analysis reports that ML models achieved the best results for classifying healthy patients (H&Y0: 95.7% to 98.2%) and DL approaches performed better for classifying higher severity levels (>92%). (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37200116/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13362068/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] One review cites a UK autopsy study that found the misdiagnosis rate of PD is 24%, and a neuroimaging review states that the heterogeneous disease phenotype and overlapping symptoms with atypical parkinsonian syndromes (APS) contribute to high misdiagnosis rates. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11112052/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11657025/
- [statement] High reported accuracy coexists with weak evidence quality: a gait meta-analysis states that its GRADE analysis revealed low-quality evidence for precision and F1 score and very-low quality for accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity, and the biomarker review reports median best-model accuracy of 95.3% while 259 studies (98.1%) were at high overall risk of bias under its adapted PROBAST rules. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13362068/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13702696/
- [statement] In a machine learning study of longitudinal clinical data from a Parkinson's progression cohort, the authors report projections of disease progression 5 years after initial diagnosis with an average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.92 for the slower progressing group and 0.95 ± 0.02 for the fast-progressing group. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9758217/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] The authors of the progression study report that they replicated their findings in an independent cohort, released the analytical code, and identified serum neurofilament light as a significant indicator of fast disease progression among other key biomarkers of interest. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9758217/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] In a UK Biobank analysis, the authors report that machine learning models trained on accelerometry data distinguished clinically diagnosed Parkinson's disease (n = 153) with an AUPRC of 0.14 ± 0.04, and prodromal Parkinson's disease (n = 113) up to 7 years pre-diagnosis with an AUPRC of 0.07 ± 0.03, from the general population (n = 33,009), outperforming models based on genetics, lifestyle, blood biochemistry or prodromal symptoms data. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37400639/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] The 95th centile of stride velocity has been approved by the EMA as a primary endpoint for assessing ambulant patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, a regulatory precedent in a disease other than Parkinson's disease. - [statement] Four reviews each point to standardization needs: a Movement Disorders systematic review of early Parkinson's disease calls for standardized study methodologies, a scoping review of prodromal Parkinson's disease says future research should prioritize standardized assessment, a real-world walking speed review says adoption requires improved standardization of devices, algorithms, and study methodologies, and a review of digital biomarkers for precision diagnosis and monitoring notes a lack of standardized data verification protocols. - [statement] In a double-blind trial of AAV2-neurturin delivered to the putamen and substantia nigra in advanced Parkinson disease, the authors report no significant difference between groups in the primary endpoint (change from baseline: AAV2-neurturin, -7.0 ± 9.92; sham, -5.2 ± 10.01; p = 0.515) among Fifty-one patients, and conclude that it was not superior to sham surgery. - [statement] A review article on clinical trials in GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease states that where GBA1 variants exert a toxic gain-of-function effect, gene therapy alone may not be sufficient, and that a strategy combining an antisense oligonucleotide with gene therapy to restore functional GBA1 may be required. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] The authors of the original case-control study hypothesize that isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a prodromal phenotype for the body-first type, and a later longitudinal study states that the presence of rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) may be indicative of a body-first pattern. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32830221/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11150376/

- [statement] Applying a pragmatic approach based on motor asymmetry, rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, and orthostatic hypotension to a large cohort of persons with early PD (disease duration <5 years), the authors report that individuals classified as probable brain-first were more often tremor-dominant and showed a trend toward less constipation after adjusting for disease duration, age and sex. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13746290/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] One meta-analysis reports that differences in microbiome structure between PD and controls are small, and a later meta-analysis states that causality cannot be established from predominantly observational studies. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-021-00156-z · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13642692/
- [statement] Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled fecal microbiota transplantation trials in Parkinson's disease report different primary-outcome results, and they differ in delivery route, comparator and primary-outcome time point: the trial at 4 hospitals in Finland (FMT or placebo via colonoscopy; primary end point at 6 months) reports that the primary outcome did not differ between the groups, whereas GUT-PARFECT (nasojejunal FMT with healthy donor stool or the participant's own stool; primary outcome at 12 months) reports that the MDS-UPDRS motor score improved by a mean of 5.8 points in the healthy donor group and by 2.7 points in the placebo group (p = 0.0235). (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11287445/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11056595/
- [statement] Studies in different cohorts report that Parkinson's disease subtypes differ in progression: one reports clusters associated with motor progression rates, another reports faster two-year progression in diffuse-malignant patients, and a third reports that data-driven subtypes exhibited the highest progression rates. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6288789/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9937525/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616926/
- [statement] The SynNeurGe classification of Parkinson's disease proposes three components, pathological α-synuclein, neurodegeneration defined by neuroimaging and pathogenic gene variants, linked to a clinical component; its authors emphasise initial application exclusively for research, and a European Academy of Neurology page lists it among two recent research frameworks for a biological definition of PD. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38267191/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://www.ean.org/research/resources/neurology-updates/detail/beyond-the-a-synuclein-seed-amplification-assay-shall-we-re-evaluate-the-biological-definition-of-parkinsons-disease
- [statement] In a preprint, the Global Parkinson's Genetics Program authors report that among 65,509 individuals with Parkinson's disease they identified 9,019 (13.8%) potentially trial-eligible genetic variant carriers, including 6,789 GBA1, 2,084 LRRK2, and 146 dual GBA1-LRRK2 carriers. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13119358/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] Two analyses of the PPMI cohort by different author groups report that LRRK2-associated Parkinson's disease includes cases negative on the CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay: one reports 46 negative and 102 positive among 148 LRRK2 parkinsonism cases, and another reports SAA-negative patients were markedly enriched for LRRK2 variants. - [statement] Reports differ on motor progression in SAA-negative Parkinson's disease: an analysis of LRRK2 carriers reports less severe motor manifestations and decline without alpha-synuclein aggregates, while a European Academy of Neurology commentary on a PPMI analysis reports faster time to motor disability milestones in SAA-negative PD, with a relatively small sample. ## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Data leakage inflates reported accuracy in PD machine learning: the neuroimaging review reports that data leakage was associated with a significant inflation of accuracies, and a separate study reports that without overt features all models exhibited superficially acceptable F1 scores but failed catastrophically in specificity, with the authors attributing high accuracy when overt features were included to data leakage rather than genuine predictive power. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11657025/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12383348/
- [statement] In a systematic review of longitudinal studies in early Parkinson's disease, the authors report that three DHTs detected longitudinal changes when scales did not, with one study showing larger effect sizes for change over time of selected DHT features compared to rating scales. (low confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30056 · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] In the brain-first versus body-first model, brain-first Parkinson's disease has α-synuclein pathology initially arising in the brain and spreading to the peripheral autonomic nervous system, while body-first Parkinson's disease has pathology originating in the enteric or peripheral autonomic nervous system and then spreading to the brain. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32830221/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11150376/
- [statement] In the case-control PET study, the authors report that RBD-positive Parkinson's disease patients and iRBD patients showed reduced mean MIBG heart:mediastinum ratios and reduced colon donepezil standard uptake values compared with RBD-negative patients, and a scientific commentary in the same journal describes the reduced gut cholinergic and cardiac noradrenergic ligand binding in both groups as major support for the body-first disease subtype. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32830221/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7821233/
- [statement] The authors of a PPMI-based analysis report that trial power simulations demonstrated that enrolling DM patients could reduce sample size requirements by approximately 50% using standard trial durations compared to unstratified PD cohorts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616926/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine
- [statement] In a PPMI analysis, the authors report that the diffuse malignant (DM) subtype had the highest GBA1 frequency, 14.0% versus 5.9% in the mild-motor predominant (MMP) subtype. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13116718/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Systematic reviews of machine learning in PD report a translation gap: one states that very few ML systems have been adopted for real-world use despite the large number of studies published every year, and a later review concludes that reported performance has advanced faster than evidence of generalizability and clinical implementation. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11112052/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease frontier platforms: dopaminergic cell replacement, gene therapy, digital biomarkers and wearables, AI, the gut-brain axis with body-first versus brain-first subtypes, and precision medicine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13702696/

## Research summary — AI and machine learning in PD diagnosis and progression

Systematic reviews of machine learning in Parkinson's disease report a translation gap: very few systems have been adopted for real-world use, external validation is uncommon and accuracy is lower on external test sets, and data leakage is associated with inflated accuracy. The reviews also report high headline accuracy alongside low-quality evidence and a high risk of bias in most assessed studies, and a preprint reports that subject-aware splitting lowers reported performance. A machine learning study of longitudinal clinical data reports projections of progression and a replication in an independent cohort. The reviews' proportions describe the samples assessed, not the whole literature.

## Research summary — Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

Wearable sensors, smartwatches and smartphone apps are studied as digital measures of Parkinson's disease for early detection, longitudinal change and regulatory endpoints. A UK Biobank accelerometry analysis reports better test performance for prodromal disease than models based on genetics, lifestyle, blood biochemistry or prodromal symptoms, and the multicenter WATCH-PD observational study reports device-derived features that differed between early Parkinson's disease and age-matched controls. Reviews report that most included studies were cross-sectional and call for standardization. A systematic review reports that no real-world walking speed measure has been fully validated by the FDA, and that a stride velocity endpoint approved by the EMA concerns a different disease. Consensus experts name the lack of clear reference values as the main challenge for digital mobility outcomes.

## Research summary — Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons

Cell replacement for Parkinson's disease transplants dopaminergic progenitor cells derived from embryonic or induced pluripotent stem cells. Recent early-phase, open-label trials of an embryonic stem cell product and an induced pluripotent stem cell product report safety findings plus exploratory motor and imaging changes, and their authors caution about small cohorts, the absence of a control group and placebo effects. In one trial the authors state that risks were primarily associated with the immunosuppression regimen. A randomized, sham surgery-controlled phase three trial of the embryonic stem cell product is registered as recruiting, and a sponsor announced a conditional, time-limited approval in Japan of an induced pluripotent stem cell product.

## Research summary — Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors

Gene therapy for Parkinson's disease uses adeno-associated viral vectors that carry genes such as GDNF, AADC, GAD and neurturin, and, in registered programmes, GBA1. The early-phase GDNF study reports safety findings and exploratory motor changes, and its authors state that a randomized controlled study is planned to confirm them. In a sham-controlled GAD trial the scores fell in both arms, with a greater fall in the gene therapy arm, while a sham-controlled neurturin trial was not superior to sham surgery. A randomized, sham-controlled GDNF study is registered, and a registry record for an intravenous GBA1 programme is withdrawn. A regulator announcement about AADC deficiency concerns a different indication.

## Research summary — Gut-brain axis: microbiome and body-first versus brain-first PD

The brain-first versus body-first model proposes that alpha-synuclein pathology in Parkinson's disease begins either in the brain or in the enteric or peripheral autonomic nervous system, and the proposers hypothesize that isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder is a prodromal phenotype of the body-first type. In their own review the proposers report that molecular imaging studies were generally in agreement with the model whereas structural imaging studies showed conflicting findings, a commentary notes limits on generalizability, and an autopsy preprint reports gut-restricted positivity in only a few subjects. Meta-analyses report gut microbiome alterations in Parkinson's disease, the authors of one state that differences in microbiome structure are small, and a later meta-analysis states that causality cannot be established. Two randomized fecal microbiota transplantation trials report different primary-outcome results.

## Research summary — PD subtypes and precision medicine

Studies in different cohorts report that Parkinson's disease subtypes differ in progression, and authors link the failure of disease-modifying trials in part to heterogeneity. Published schemes include data-driven clusters and the SynNeurGe research classification, which combines pathological alpha-synuclein, neurodegeneration defined by neuroimaging and pathogenic gene variants. Authors report that replication of published subtype classifications is limited. A genetic consortium preprint reports many potentially trial-eligible carriers of GBA1 and LRRK2 variants. Sponsors state that the LRRK2 kinase inhibitor BIIB122 did not meet its endpoints in an early-stage study that included people with or without a pathogenic LRRK2 variant and that they will discontinue development in idiopathic disease, while a study in carriers continues. Reports differ on motor progression in seed amplification assay negative disease.
